{
  "title": "CompLocoGen: Dynamics-Aware Compositional Task Generation for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation",
  "core_problem": "Scaling humanoid loco-manipulation to diverse real-world tasks requires diverse training environments, but every loco-manipulation task in NVIDIA's AGILE/GR00T-WBC ecosystem must be manually specified as a self-contained Isaac Lab configuration file (scene, observations, actions, rewards, terminations, curriculum) with hand-designed stage-weighted reward functions. VIRAL (CVPR 2026) demonstrates individual composite tasks work but identifies reward engineering as a scaling bottleneck. LLM-based reward design methods (STRIDE, FORGE/EUREKA) automate reward optimization for single predefined tasks but cannot generate compositionally coupled multi-stage tasks where inter-primitive dynamics (balance during walk-to-pick transitions, gait adaptation for carry, CoM shifts at primitive boundaries) create emergent failure modes absent from any individual primitive. How can we automatically compose diverse, dynamically feasible loco-manipulation task configurations—generating Isaac Lab-compatible environment specifications from a physics-informed skill grammar—to produce training data for task compositions that no human has manually designed?",
  "opportunity": "VIRAL (CVPR 2026) achieves 54 consecutive real-world loco-manipulation cycles on G1 but relies entirely on hand-designed stage-weighted rewards—the authors themselves state that 'scaling to the open-ended diversity of daily life remains intractable' via manual reward engineering. STRIDE (arXiv:2502.04692) and FORGE (OpenReview 2025) automate reward design for single-task locomotion (STRIDE: 250% over EUREKA) and single-task RL (FORGE: 38.5% over EUREKA on Humanoid), but both operate on individual predefined tasks—they cannot generate novel multi-stage task compositions where the coupling between primitives creates emergent physical challenges. LHM-Humanoid (arXiv:2508.16943) achieves impressive long-horizon loco-manipulation across 350 scenes but relies on manually designed scene/task configurations. AGILE (arXiv:2603.20147, open-source at github.com/nvidia-isaac/WBC-AGILE) provides a configuration-driven Isaac Lab workflow where every task is a self-contained file specifying the complete MDP—but only manual authoring is supported. Isaac Lab Issue #5278 (April 2026) proposes LLM-generated environments for rigid-body manipulation only, not coupled loco-manipulation. The gap is precise: no system automatically generates compositionally coupled loco-manipulation task configurations with physics-informed feasibility guarantees. The key insight is that compositional task generation is fundamentally different from per-task reward optimization: STRIDE/FORGE optimize rewards for one task at a time, but coupled loco-manipulation introduces inter-primitive dynamics (balance shifts during transitions, gait adaptation under load, grasp stability during locomotion) that only emerge during composition and cannot be addressed by iterating on individual task rewards. All infrastructure components exist—pre-trained SONIC locomotion checkpoints, PinkKinematics IK, AGILE's configuration-driven framework, 4096 parallel GPU environments—but no automated composer connects them with dynamics-aware feasibility filtering.",
  "landscape": "**LLM-based reward design (per-task optimization)**: STRIDE (arXiv:2502.04692, Feb 2025) automates reward design for humanoid locomotion via LLMs with iterative refinement, outperforming EUREKA by 250% on sprint tasks across complex terrains—but limited to single-task locomotion, no manipulation, no compositional coupling. FORGE (OpenReview 2025) uses multi-agent LLMs for evolutionary reward refinement with 38.5% gains on Humanoid—also single-task, withdrawn from review. EUREKA (ICLR 2024) established the LLM-to-reward-code-to-evaluate-to-refine paradigm for 29 environments. These methods solve reward engineering for individual tasks; CompLocoGen solves the orthogonal problem of composing novel multi-stage tasks where inter-primitive dynamics create emergent challenges that per-task reward optimization cannot discover. **Data/trajectory generation approaches**: GR00T-Gen (NVIDIA, 2025) generates 100+ individual tasks via LLMs but treats manipulation, locomotion, and navigation as separate categories—not compositionally coupled. DreamGen/GR00T-Dreams (arXiv:2505.12705) generates synthetic manipulation trajectories via video world models, bounded by seed demonstration diversity. HumanoidGen (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2507.00833) uses LLM+MCTS for fixed-base bimanual manipulation demonstrations. GenManip (CVPR 2025) provides LLM-driven simulation for generalizable manipulation task generation—tabletop only, establishes the LLM-to-simulation-to-filter paradigm we extend to dynamics-aware loco-manipulation. RoboGen (ICML 2024) uses LLMs for single-arm task generation. The Isaac Lab LLM Environment Pipeline (GitHub Issue #5278, April 2026) proposes two-stage LLM generation of Isaac Lab environments but only for rigid-body manipulation, using custom JSON, not loco-manipulation. **Sim-to-real and composite task approaches**: VIRAL/GR00T-VisualSim2Real (CVPR 2026, NVlabs open-source) demonstrates composite loco-manipulation (Walk-Stand-Drop-Grasp-Turn cycles) on G1 with 54 consecutive real-world cycles—but tasks are hand-designed via stage-weighted reward functions; the authors explicitly identify 'reward engineering bottleneck' as preventing scaling. This is the strongest existing loco-manipulation result and our primary comparison: we automate what VIRAL currently requires manual engineering for. **Long-horizon loco-manipulation approaches**: LHM-Humanoid (arXiv:2508.16943, updated March 2026) learns unified policies for long-horizon loco-manipulation across 350 diverse scenes (4 room types, 79 objects) via RL teacher distillation with DAgger—achieves strong cross-scene generalization but relies on manually designed scene configurations. CompLocoGen could serve as an automated scene/task generator for LHM-Humanoid-style policy learning. WholeBodyVLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2512.11047) learns unified latent VLA for loco-manipulation from action-free egocentric videos with loco-manipulation-oriented RL—a policy architecture contribution orthogonal to our task generation focus. FALCON (arXiv:2505.06776, L4DC 2026) demonstrates force-adaptive dual-agent RL for loco-manipulation (payload transport 0-20N, cart-pulling 0-100N, door-opening 0-40N) on real humanoids—validates that coupled loco-manipulation is deployable but uses hand-designed tasks. **Trajectory generation alternatives**: 'Physically Consistent Humanoid Loco-Manipulation using Latent Diffusion Models' (arXiv:2504.16843, Humanoids 2025) generates RGB scenes via LDMs then extracts contacts for whole-body trajectory optimization—an alternative generation paradigm using vision-guided planning rather than grammar-constrained composition; limited by LDM scene diversity and requires expensive trajectory optimization per scenario. **Skill composition approaches**: Humanoid Hanoi (arXiv:2602.13850, Feb 2026) demonstrates distribution shift during skill composition requiring data aggregation under domain randomization; directly informs our dynamics-aware transition modeling. SkillBlender (arXiv:2506.09366) validates compositional skill blending on G1 in legged_gym (not Isaac Lab), requiring manual specification. **Simulation infrastructure**: AGILE (arXiv:2603.20147, March 2026, github.com/nvidia-isaac/WBC-AGILE, Apache 2.0) provides the target substrate—a comprehensive Isaac Lab workflow where every task is a self-contained configuration file specifying scene, observations, actions, rewards, terminations, and curriculum. AGILE's configuration-driven architecture enables MDP parameters to be modified without structural code changes. Critically, AGILE's YAML descriptors are deployment I/O contracts (joint names, observation ordering, action scaling, history buffers) for sim-to-sim/sim-to-real transfer—NOT training task specifications. Training tasks use Isaac Lab's Python @configclass manager-based workflow. CompLocoGen generates Isaac Lab configuration files in this format, NOT YAML deployment descriptors. GR00T-WBC/SONIC (NVlabs, open-source Apache 2.0) provides pre-trained G1 locomotion checkpoints trained on 142K+ motions. **The specific gap**: No system automatically generates compositionally coupled loco-manipulation task configurations with dynamics-aware feasibility filtering. STRIDE/FORGE automate single-task reward design but cannot compose multi-stage tasks. LHM-Humanoid achieves long-horizon loco-manipulation but with manually designed scenes. VIRAL achieves real-world composite tasks but with hand-engineered rewards. CompLocoGen fills this gap with a physics-informed grammar that encodes dynamic feasibility constraints and generates Isaac Lab-compatible task configurations for the AGILE/GR00T-WBC ecosystem.",
  "approach": "We build CompLocoGen as a dynamics-aware compositional task generator that produces Isaac Lab-compatible loco-manipulation task configurations via a physics-informed skill grammar, frontier LLM, and pre-trained GR00T-WBC infrastructure—all within 200 H100-hours.\n\n**Physics-Informed Skill Grammar with Dynamic Feasibility Constraints**: We define a formal context-free grammar over four coupled loco-manipulation primitives—walk(target_pos, speed, gait_style), pick(object_id, grasp_type, approach_vector), place(target_pos, placement_constraint), carry(object_id, carry_pose, stability_mode)—each with typed spatial parameters and two levels of constraints: (1) Structural preconditions/postconditions (carry requires pick.postcondition=grasped)—filtering structurally impossible sequences before LLM generation. (2) Dynamic feasibility predicates computed from simplified analytical physics models: ZMP margin analysis for balance during primitive transitions (e.g., walk-to-pick requires bending that shifts CoM—verify ZMP stays within support polygon given walk speed and object height), centroidal dynamics for load-dependent gait feasibility (carry(mass) + walk(speed) must satisfy that the required joint torques stay within G1's actuator limits, estimated via simplified inverted pendulum model with payload), and force-closure bounds for grasp stability during locomotion (lateral acceleration during turning while carrying must not exceed grasp friction cone). Unlike STRIDE/FORGE, which optimize rewards for a single predefined task, the grammar encodes inter-primitive coupling constraints: the feasibility of carry(5kg) + walk(1.2m/s) depends jointly on both primitives and the transition dynamics between them—something no per-task reward optimizer can discover because it never composes tasks. Unlike GenManip/RoboGen/HumanoidGen's unconstrained LLM generation, the physics-informed grammar prevents both structurally impossible AND dynamically infeasible compositions BEFORE simulation, reducing wasted compute. The dynamic feasibility predicates are intentionally analytical (not learned), making them interpretable, requiring no training data, and providing physically meaningful failure explanations.\n\n**LLM-Guided Task Program Generation with Isaac Lab Compilation**: The LLM (Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B) generates task programs as grammar-valid primitive sequences with spatial parameter bindings, constrained by both structural and dynamic feasibility predicates. The LLM reasons about task semantics (multi-object delivery routes, obstacle-aware transport, sequential pickup schedules) while the grammar enforces physical validity. Generated task programs are then compiled into Isaac Lab Python @configclass environment configurations using AGILE's configuration-driven architecture as the template: each generated task becomes a self-contained configuration file specifying scene setup (object positions, obstacles, goal locations), observation space, action space, staged reward functions (following VIRAL's stage-weighted approach but auto-generated from primitive sequence structure), termination conditions, and curriculum parameters. This compilation layer is our contribution—it bridges the grammar's abstract task programs to Isaac Lab's concrete environment specification format. We do NOT generate AGILE YAML deployment descriptors; we generate the upstream training task configurations that AGILE's workflow consumes.\n\n**Pre-trained GR00T-WBC Execution**: Instead of training locomotion from scratch (saving 50-100 H100-hours), we use GR00T-WBC's decoupled architecture: the pre-trained SONIC locomotion checkpoint (HuggingFace, trained on 142K+ G1-retargeted motions) controls lower-body joints, while PinkKinematics IK (from Isaac Lab PRs #3150/#3259) controls upper-body manipulation. A state-machine coordinator executes generated task programs by sequencing SONIC locomotion commands and IK targets based on primitive transitions. For carry-specific gaits not well-covered by the base SONIC checkpoint, we fine-tune with <5 H100-hours using AGILE's training pipeline.\n\n**Simulation Verification with Dynamics Predicate Calibration**: Each generated configuration is instantiated in Isaac Lab (4096 parallel environments) and executed. Physics verification checks: (1) CoM balance maintenance throughout, with specific attention to primitive transition points (informed by Humanoid Hanoi's distribution-shift finding), (2) grasp stability during locomotion phases via force threshold monitoring, (3) collision avoidance, (4) task completion criteria. Critically, simulation results feed back to calibrate the analytical dynamics predicates: when the ZMP predictor says a composition is feasible but simulation shows balance failure, we tighten the predictor's safety margins for that transition type. This online calibration improves the grammar's filtering accuracy over the generation campaign without requiring a separate training phase. Failed programs also receive structured LLM feedback mapping failure modes to grammar parameter adjustments. The yield rate (fraction of generated compositions that pass physics verification) is reported as an experimental metric—we do not assume a specific rate a priori. The comparison between dynamics-aware yield and structural-only yield is a key ablation.\n\n**Downstream Evaluation with Compositional Generalization Focus**: Train a diffusion policy (ACT architecture, proven on G1 in GR00T ecosystem) on generated datasets. Evaluate compositional generalization: (a) held-out task compositions (primitive sequences not in training set), (b) held-out spatial configurations (same task type, novel object positions), (c) held-out dynamic parameters (same composition structure, novel mass/speed combinations). Baselines: (1) STRIDE-style per-task iterative reward generation—for each composed task, apply STRIDE's LLM reward optimization pipeline to test whether per-task reward tuning suffices for compositional tasks, (2) Grammar-only composition (structural constraints, no dynamics predicates)—ablates the value of dynamics-aware filtering, (3) LLM-only generation without grammar constraints—tests whether the grammar adds value over free-form LLM task generation, (4) LHM-Humanoid-style manually designed task set (5-8 hand-designed composite tasks matching VIRAL complexity), (5) Random grammar sampling without LLM semantic reasoning. The central claim is that compositionally diverse generated data enables generalization to novel task configurations unachievable by any per-task or manual approach—and that dynamics-aware filtering specifically targets the inter-primitive coupling failures that make loco-manipulation composition uniquely challenging.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["MISSING COMPETING WORK: Eurekaverse (CoRL 2024, NVIDIA Research) establishes LLM-driven environment curriculum generation with agent-environment co-evolution for RL training. While it targets quadrupedal parkour (not humanoid loco-manipulation), the paradigm—LLM generates diverse training environments, train policies, evaluate, feed back to LLM for next iteration—is essentially identical to CompLocoGen's pipeline. This must be cited and explicitly differentiated: Eurekaverse generates environment variations for single-skill training; CompLocoGen generates compositionally coupled multi-stage task configurations with inter-primitive dynamics constraints.", "MISSING BASELINE: DemoHLM (arXiv:2510.11258) generates diverse humanoid loco-manipulation trajectories from a single teleoperated demonstration by converting to object-centric representations and replaying under varied initial conditions. It uses a 3-stage pipeline (locomotion → pre-manipulation → manipulation) with a hierarchical controller on Unitree G1. While DemoHLM generates spatial variations of one task template rather than compositionally novel tasks, it should be added as a data-generation baseline to demonstrate that grammar-based composition produces qualitatively different (not just more) training data than demo-augmentation approaches.", "VENUE MISMATCH: The user explicitly targets CoRL 2026 (paper deadline May 29, 19 days away). The proposal honestly pivots to Humanoids 2026 (July 24, 75 days) as primary target. While this honesty is appreciated, the proposal must either: (a) commit to a minimal CoRL submission (2-3 task compositions, pre-trained everything, single downstream eval, no ablation depth) with Humanoids as the full version, or (b) clearly justify why CoRL is infeasible and Humanoids is the right venue. Currently the proposal lists Humanoids as primary but doesn't address how to satisfy the user's CoRL requirement.", "LIMITED COMPOSITIONAL SPACE: The grammar defines only 4 primitives (walk, pick, place, carry). The number of meaningfully distinct task compositions from 4 primitives is inherently limited. With structural and dynamic feasibility filtering, the effective compositional space may be quite small. The proposal should either (a) expand primitives (push, pull, open_door, climb_stairs, squat) to demonstrate the grammar's extensibility, or (b) provide analysis of how many compositionally distinct and dynamically feasible tasks the 4-primitive grammar can produce.", "NOVELTY DEPTH FOR CoRL: The technical contribution reduces to (1) a context-free grammar over 4 primitives with typed parameters and analytical physics predicates, (2) LLM-guided constrained generation with Qwen 3.6, (3) compilation to Isaac Lab @configclass, (4) rejection sampling with online predicate calibration. Each component individually uses standard techniques. The combination is novel for loco-manipulation, but CoRL reviewers may expect deeper algorithmic contribution—e.g., learning the dynamics predicates from data rather than hand-coding ZMP/centroidal analysis, or providing formal guarantees about compositional coverage/completeness. For Humanoids 2026, this systems contribution would be appropriately valued.", "GENIE SIM 3.0 (arXiv:2601.02078, AgiBot, Jan 2026) is a comprehensive simulation platform with LLM-powered scene generation that generates thousands of diverse environments for humanoid robots across 200+ tasks. While it focuses on scene construction rather than compositional task specification with physics constraints, it represents a relevant large-scale automated generation approach and should be briefly acknowledged in the landscape."]
Feedback: The proposal has improved substantially across rounds 1-3 (compute budget fixed, AGILE configclass corrected, STRIDE/FORGE differentiated, yield rate as experimental metric). The core idea—dynamics-aware compositional grammar for humanoid loco-manipulation task generation—is genuinely valuable and addresses a real bottleneck. Three targeted changes would bring this to pass quality:

1. **ADD EUREKAVERSE AND DemoHLM**: Eurekaverse (CoRL 2024) is the most important missing citation—it pioneered LLM-driven environment curriculum generation. Your differentiation is clear (single-skill environment variation vs. compositional multi-stage task generation with inter-primitive dynamics constraints) but must be explicitly stated. DemoHLM should be added as a data-generation baseline to show that compositional generation produces qualitatively different training data than demo augmentation.

2. **RESOLVE VENUE STRATEGY**: Either (a) commit to a minimal CoRL abstract (May 26, 16 days): 4 primitives, 3-5 task compositions using pre-trained SONIC+IK, single downstream eval, no ablations—essentially a proof-of-concept showing the grammar works—with full paper at Humanoids 2026; OR (b) drop CoRL and commit fully to Humanoids 2026 with full scope. A split strategy (CoRL abstract as teaser, Humanoids as full paper) is viable if the pipeline can produce initial results in ~14 days.

3. **EXPAND GRAMMAR OR JUSTIFY SCOPE**: Either add 2-3 more primitives (push, open_door, squat) to demonstrate extensibility, or provide explicit analysis of compositional diversity: how many unique task programs does the 4-primitive grammar produce? What fraction survive structural filtering? Dynamic filtering? This strengthens the contribution by quantifying the grammar's generative power.

Minor: Add Genie Sim 3.0 to landscape (LLM-driven scene generation, different scope but related). Consider whether learning dynamics predicates (small MLP trained on simulation rollouts) rather than purely analytical models could provide an additional novelty dimension for CoRL framing.

## Instructions
- Think in two phases: FIRST reconsider the problem framing (core_problem / opportunity / landscape) if the reviewer flagged issues there, THEN revise the method (approach / resource_estimate / key_references). Do not jump straight to fixing the method if the underlying problem framing needs correction.
- Address each issue specifically.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？
   - 修订后的 idea 相比上一版有什么本质性的改进？

4. **避免表面修订**：如果你发现自己只是在换措辞或补充细节而没有实质改进，
   考虑是否需要 major revision 或 pivot。反复的 minor fix 不会拯救一个根基有问题的 idea。

## 针对 Review 意见的定向搜索

对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，执行以下搜索流程：

1. **如果 reviewer 说'已有类似工作'**：
   - 搜索 reviewer 提到的论文，用 WebFetch 实际阅读
   - 搜索该论文的 cited-by，找到后续跟进工作
   - 明确你的 idea 与这些工作的差异化点——如果差异化不够，必须 pivot

2. **如果 reviewer 说'SOTA 过时'**：
   - 用 Papers With Code 查看当前排行榜
   - 搜索过去 6 个月的最新方法
   - 更新你的 landscape 和 baseline

## Genie Sim 3.0 (arXiv:2601.02078) -- Detailed Summary

### What It Is

Genie Sim 3.0 is a high-fidelity, open-source simulation platform for humanoid robot manipulation developed by AgiBot (AGIBOT Innovation, Shanghai). Unveiled at CES 2026 in January, it is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Omniverse and addresses three core bottlenecks in embodied AI: environment generation, data scalability, and standardized evaluation. Its stated goal is to make synthetic simulation data an effective substitute for expensive real-world data collection for scalable robot policy training.

---

### How It Uses LLMs for Scene Generation (Genie Sim Generator)

The LLM-powered scene generation pipeline operates through four sequential stages:

1. **Intention Interpreter** -- A chain-of-thought-enabled LLM parses natural language scene descriptions into structured JSON schemas containing semantic object classes, geometric constraints, and spatial relations.

2. **Assets Index** -- A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module encodes 5,140 simulation-ready objects (across 353 categories) into a vector database using QWEN text-embedding-v4. Semantic search returns top-k candidate assets with metadata in approximately 200 ms.

3. **DSL Code Generator** -- A pre-trained LLM synthesizes a domain-specific language (DSL) program compatible with Isaac Sim, providing fine-grained controllability with double-float precision for object placement.

4. **Results Assembler** -- Instantiates the DSL program into hierarchical scene graphs (nodes = objects, edges = spatial relations), generating thousands of diverse scenes within minutes through systematic domain randomization across lighting, layout, camera noise, robot pose, and scene configuration.

The pipeline can produce entire environments from conversational natural-language input, eliminating manual scene authoring.

---

### Scale: Tasks and Environments

- **200+ tasks** spanning robotic manipulation
- **10,000+ hours** of synthetic training data in the open-source dataset
- **100,000+ evaluation scenarios** in the Genie Sim Benchmark
- **5,140 simulation-ready 3D assets** across 353 object categories
- Scene generation produces **thousands of diverse scenes within minutes**

Environment reconstruction also uses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with camera pose optimization (SuperPoint + LightGlue), and diffusion-model-based view extrapolation for incomplete captures.

---

### Supported Robots and Models

- **Humanoid robots**: Genie G1, Genie G2
- **End effectors**: Omnipicker, Omnihands, INSPIRE Skillhands, Zhixing Gripper
- **Compatible Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models evaluated**: pi-0.5, GO-1, UniVLA, RDT, X-VLA
- **Data collection modes**: Teleoperation via PICO VR headset, and automated collection via cuRobo motion planner

---

### Limitations Regarding Compositional Task Specification

The paper and surrounding coverage reveal several notable limitations:

1. **Incomplete autonomy in scene generation** -- The system requires explicit feedback loops with users for clarification when natural language constraints contradict system rules. It does not gracefully handle ambiguous or contradictory instructions autonomously.

2. **Performance degrades with task complexity** -- Success rates drop significantly for compositional/long-horizon tasks. The "Organize Objects" task (a multi-step compositional task) achieved only ~52% success with 1,500 synthetic episodes, compared to ~80% for simpler atomic grasping tasks. The paper evaluates "atomic skill operation" and "long-horizon task composition" but provides no detailed mechanism for how multi-step tasks are decomposed, sequenced, or specified compositionally.

3. **No explicit compositional task grammar** -- The paper does not describe a formal compositional task specification language or a principled way to combine atomic skills into complex behaviors. Long-horizon task composition is evaluated but not architecturally formalized.

Genie Sim 3.0 represents a significant advance in automated simulation environment generation through LLMs, but its compositional task specification remains implicit rather than formally defined. LeVERB (Latent Vision-Language-Encoded Robot Behavior) is a hierarchical latent instruction-following framework for humanoid vision-language whole-body control, the first of its kind.

Vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong semantic understanding and zero-shot generalization, yet most existing systems assume an accurate low-level controller with hand-crafted action "vocabulary" such as end-effector pose or root velocity, confining prior work to quasi-static tasks and precluding the agile, whole-body behaviors required by humanoid whole-body control tasks.

## Genie Sim 3.0 (arXiv:2601.02078) -- Detailed Summary

### What It Is

Genie Sim 3.0 is a high-fidelity, open-source simulation platform for humanoid robot manipulation developed by AgiBot (AGIBOT Innovation, Shanghai). Unveiled at CES 2026 in January, it is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim / Omniverse and addresses three core bottlenecks in embodied AI: environment generation, data scalability, and standardized evaluation. Its stated goal is to make synthetic simulation data an effective substitute for expensive real-world data collection for scalable robot policy training.

---

### How It Uses LLMs for Scene Generation (Genie Sim Generator)

The LLM-powered scene generation pipeline operates through four sequential stages:

1. **Intention Interpreter** -- A chain-of-thought-enabled LLM parses natural language scene descriptions into structured JSON schemas containing semantic object classes, geometric constraints, and spatial relations.

2. **Assets Index** -- A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) module encodes 5,140 simulation-ready objects (across 353 categories) into a vector database using QWEN text-embedding-v4. Semantic search returns top-k candidate assets with metadata in approximately 200 ms.

3. **DSL Code Generator** -- A pre-trained LLM synthesizes a domain-specific language (DSL) program compatible with Isaac Sim, providing fine-grained controllability with double-float precision for object placement.

4. **Results Assembler** -- Instantiates the DSL program into hierarchical scene graphs (nodes = objects, edges = spatial relations), generating thousands of diverse scenes within minutes through systematic domain randomization across lighting, layout, camera noise, robot pose, and scene configuration.

The pipeline can produce entire environments from conversational natural-language input, eliminating manual scene authoring.

---

### Scale: Tasks and Environments

- **200+ tasks** spanning robotic manipulation
- **10,000+ hours** of synthetic training data in the open-source dataset
- **100,000+ evaluation scenarios** in the Genie Sim Benchmark
- **5,140 simulation-ready 3D assets** across 353 object categories
- Scene generation produces **thousands of diverse scenes within minutes**

Environment reconstruction also uses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with camera pose optimization (SuperPoint + LightGlue), and diffusion-model-based view extrapolation for incomplete captures.

---

### Supported Robots and Models

- **Humanoid robots**: Genie G1, Genie G2
- **End effectors**: Omnipicker, Omnihands, INSPIRE Skillhands, Zhixing Gripper
- **Compatible Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models evaluated**: pi-0.5, GO-1, UniVLA, RDT, X-VLA
- **Data collection modes**: Teleoperation via PICO VR headset, and automated collection via cuRobo motion planner

---

### Limitations Regarding Compositional Task Specification

The paper and surrounding coverage reveal several notable limitations:

1. **Incomplete autonomy in scene generation** -- The system requires explicit feedback loops with users for clarification when natural language constraints contradict system rules. It does not gracefully handle ambiguous or contradictory instructions autonomously.

2. **Performance degrades with task complexity** -- Success rates drop significantly for compositional/long-horizon tasks. The "Organize Objects" task (a multi-step compositional task) achieved only ~52% success with 1,500 synthetic episodes, compared to ~80% for simpler atomic grasping tasks. The paper evaluates "atomic skill operation" and "long-horizon task composition" but provides no detailed mechanism for how multi-step tasks are decomposed, sequenced, or specified compositionally.

3. **No explicit compositional task grammar** -- The paper does not describe a formal compositional task specification language or a principled way to combine atomic skills into complex behaviors. Long-horizon task composition is evaluated but not architecturally formalized.

4. **Real data still outperforms synthetic at equivalent scale** -- Models trained on 500 real-world episodes consistently outperformed models trained on equivalent synthetic data, indicating the sim-to-real gap remains meaningful.

5. **Sim-to-real gap persists** -- Minor discrepancies remain due to approximations in contact dynamics and friction modeling, plus stochastic real-world factors.

6. **3DGS reconstruction limitations** -- Complex indoor environments showed insufficient camera pose accuracy, requiring diffusion-model view extrapolation as a workaround.

7. **No ablation of language-understanding failures** -- The paper does not systematically study what kinds of natural language descriptions the scene generator cannot handle, nor does it quantify degradation under compositionally complex or ambiguous prompts.

---

### Key Takeaway

Genie Sim 3.0 represents a significant advance in automated simulation environment generation through LLMs, but its compositional task specification remains implicit rather than formally defined. The system excels at generating diverse scenes for atomic manipulation skills but struggles with complex multi-step tasks, and the paper lacks a principled framework for specifying, decomposing, or verifying compositional task structures from language.

## DemoHLM: From One Demonstration to Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

**arXiv: 2510.11258**
**Authors:** Yuhui Fu, Feiyang Xie, Chaoyi Xu, Jing Xiong, Haoqi Yuan, and Zongqing Lu

---

### What is DemoHLM?

DemoHLM is a framework that enables a humanoid robot to learn generalizable loco-manipulation skills from a **single teleoperated demonstration** captured in simulation. From that one demo, it automatically synthesizes hundreds to thousands of diverse successful trajectories by replaying the demonstration under varied initial conditions, then trains imitation learning policies on this synthetic data that transfer zero-shot to the real world.

---

### Pipeline Overview (Hierarchical Architecture)

DemoHLM uses a **two-level hierarchy**:

1. **Low-level universal whole-body controller** -- takes motion commands (linear velocities vx/vy, yaw rate omega, torso height/roll/pitch/yaw, upper-body joint targets) and outputs joint-level PD targets at 50 Hz, providing omnidirectional locomotion.

2. **High-level manipulation policy** -- learned via behavior cloning on the generated data, using visual feedback from an RGB-D camera to produce commands for the whole-body controller.

---

### Object-Centric Representation Conversion

The key insight enabling data generation from a single demo is converting the demonstration into **object-centric relative pose trajectories**:

- The demonstration is split at the **first contact time** (tc) into two segments.
- **Before contact (object-centric phase):** End-effector poses are expressed relative to the object: `T_obj_eef = T_eef * (T_obj_bar)^{-1}`. This means the approach trajectory is defined relative to the object, so when the object moves, the end-effector trajectory adapts accordingly.
- **After contact (proprioception-centric phase):** End-effector poses are expressed relative to the end-effector's pose at the contact moment: `T_pro_eef = T_eef * (T_eef_bar)_{tc}^{-1}`. This handles the manipulation phase where the hand remains roughly fixed relative to the object.

These relative representations allow the same demonstration to be "replayed" for arbitrary initial robot and object poses.

---

### The 3-Stage Trajectory Generation Pipeline

For each new randomized initial condition, a trajectory is generated in three stages:

1. **Locomotion Stage:** A PD controller generates velocity commands (vx, vy, omega_yaw) to navigate the robot's base from its random initial pose to a suitable starting position near the object. The stage terminates when distance and rotation thresholds are met.

2. **Pre-Manipulation Stage:** Using the object-centric representation, the system computes target end-effector poses as `T_eef = T_obj_eef * T_obj_bar`. An interpolation trajectory smoothly bridges any gap between the current end-effector pose (after locomotion) and the required starting pose for manipulation. This ensures the hand is correctly positioned relative to the object regardless of approach direction.

3. **Manipulation Stage:** Switches to the proprioception-centric representation. End-effector poses are computed as `T_eef = T_eef_bar * (T_pro_eef)^{-1}`. The controller executes the actual manipulation skill (lifting, pushing, grasping, etc.).

---

### VR Teleoperation Setup

- An **Apple Vision Pro** is used as the motion capture device via the VisionProTeleop system.
- It streams head and wrist poses, which are mapped to the G1's corresponding head and wrist links.
- Lower-body degrees of freedom remain fixed during collection.
- Multi-task inverse kinematics (using the **Pink library**) solves for full-body joint targets.

---

### Robot Platform

**Unitree G1 humanoid robot** equipped with:
- An RGB-D camera for visual feedback
- Both rubber-hand and gripper end-effectors (tested across different task sets)

---

### Experimental Results

**10 loco-manipulation tasks tested:**
- Rubber-hand tasks (4): LiftBox, PressCube, PushCube, Handover
- Gripper tasks (6): GraspCube, OpenCabinet, PushCart, EraseBoard, PourWater, ExchangeCube

**Data scaling:** Success rates increase monotonically with dataset size (100 to 5000 trajectories), with diminishing returns at larger scales. Example: LiftBox went from 86.41% (100 samples) to 98.83% (5000 samples).

**Behavior cloning architectures compared:**
- **ACT** (Action Chunking Transformers) and **Diffusion Policy** achieved comparable strong performance
- **MLP** with action chunking showed substantial drops, suggesting temporally expressive architectures are important

**Randomization regions (R1-R3):** Larger spatial randomization introduces more variability but reduces data generation success rates. R3 (largest) is used by default.

**Real-world validation:** 5 trials per task on the physical Unitree G1, demonstrating robust sim-to-real transfer.

---

### Limitations (Acknowledged by Authors)

1. **Sim-to-real gap:** Reliance on simulation-generated data can hinder real robot performance due to domain differences.
2. **Limited perception:** A single RGB-D camera may constrain performance in cluttered or occluded scenes.
3. **Object pose dependence:** Using FoundationPose for 6D object pose estimation limits manipulation to pre-modeled objects only (cannot handle unmodeled/novel objects).

---

### Relationship to Grammar-Based Compositional Task Generation

The paper does **not** mention or compare against grammar-based compositional task generation approaches. DemoHLM's approach is fundamentally different from grammar-based methods:

- **Grammar-based approaches** (e.g., task and motion planning with symbolic grammars) define tasks through compositional rules and symbolic primitives, generating diverse tasks by combining grammar elements.
- **DemoHLM** instead takes a **data-driven demonstration-centric** approach -- it does not compose new tasks from primitives but rather generates diverse *instances* of the same task by varying spatial configurations. The "diversity" is in the initial conditions and object placements, not in task structure.

DemoHLM is conceptually an extension of **MimicGen** (which worked only with fixed-base robot arms) to the full humanoid loco-manipulation setting, adding the locomotion stage and handling the unique challenges of whole-body control.

---

### Key Differentiators from Prior Work

| Prior approach | DemoHLM's advantage |
|---|---|
| RL with task-specific rewards (WoCoCo, etc.) | No reward engineering needed |
| Large real-world teleoperation datasets | Only one demo required |
| MimicGen (fixed-base arms) | Handles full humanoid locomotion + manipulation |
| SMPL-based motion retargeting | Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer |
| Hard-coded task definitions | Automatically generalizes from demonstration |

---

## Summary of Findings

This is an **active and rapidly maturing research area** (2023-2025), with multiple complementary approaches. There is clearly prior work here, but the space is not saturated -- especially for humanoid-specific applications and for learning dynamics predicates that replace analytical models like ZMP/centroidal dynamics.

---

## 1. Learned Models That Predict Whether a Skill Sequence Will Succeed

### Generative Skill Chaining (GSC) -- Mishra et al., 2024 (CoRL/arXiv)
The most directly relevant work. It trains **skill-level diffusion models** that capture the joint distribution of (precondition, skill parameters, effect) for each skill. At inference time, it samples valid skill chains by ensuring each skill's post-condition satisfies the next skill's precondition. This **implicitly predicts transition feasibility** -- if the chained sampling fails to find a valid configuration, the sequence is deemed infeasible.

- Paper: [Generative Skill Chaining: Long-Horizon Skill Planning with Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03360)
- Project: [https://generative-skill-chaining.github.io/](https://generative-skill-chaining.github.io/)

### SCaR: Refining Skill Chaining for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation (NeurIPS 2024)
Refines skill chaining with learned success predictors that determine whether sub-task transitions will lead to overall task success.

- Paper: [SCaR (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/ca92ff06d973ece92cecc561757d500e-Paper-Conference.pdf)

### Skill Transformer / MuST (Multi-Head Skill Transformer)
Transformers trained end-to-end on demonstration trajectories to predict both high-level skill selection and low-level actions. MuST maintains 80-90% success rates on 40 evaluation tasks and learns to select optimal skill orderings (e.g., "pick first" vs. "flip first") depending on object state.

- [Skill Transformer (arXiv 2308.09873)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09873)
- [MuST (Amazon Science)](https://cdn.amazon.science/fd/a2/6f07a8c241fcad2a93a5bb889428/must-multi-head-skill-transformer-for-long-horizon-dexterous-manipulation-with-skill-progress.pdf)

### ConditionNET (2025)
Learns preconditions and effects of actions in a **fully data-driven manner** using vision-language models, explicitly modeling dependencies between actions, preconditions, and effects for execution monitoring.

- Paper: [ConditionNET (arXiv 2502.01167)](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01167)

---

## 2. Approaches That Learn Transition Dynamics Between Primitives

### SuperDyno (ICLR 2025 Workshop)
**Directly relevant to your reviewer's suggestion.** Learns a differentiable neural dynamics model for humanoid whole-body control. Medium-sized neural networks serve as a differentiable simulator, providing smoother gradients than analytical simulators, enabling escape from local optima, and supporting domain transfer. This replaces analytical dynamics with learned ones.

- Paper: [SuperDyno: Scalable Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Differentiable Neural Network Dynamics](https://dynamics-humanoid.github.io/dynamics-humanoid/)
- OpenReview: [ICLR 2025 Workshop](https://openreview.net/forum?id=FPgKt7bA8w)

### SRSA: Skill Retrieval and Adaptation (2024)
Learns a **transfer success predictor** that takes source/target task features (geometry, dynamics, expert actions) as input and outputs zero-shot transfer success probability. This is essentially a learned feasibility classifier for skill reuse.

- Project: [SRSA](https://srsa2024.github.io/)

### Relational Learning for Skill Preconditions (CMU Robotics Institute)
Learns an **object-relation model** with continuous representations for pairwise object relations, trained in simulation and used by a separate precondition model to predict real-world skill preconditions. Generalizes to variable numbers of objects with different shapes/sizes.

- Paper: [Relational Learning for Skill Preconditions](https://www.ri.cmu.edu/publications/relational-learning-for-skill-preconditions/)

---

## 3. GNN and Transformer-Based Composition Feasibility Predictors

### GSC: Graph-based Skill Composition (Robotics and Autonomous Systems, Sep 2024)
The most directly relevant GNN-based work. Models **entire skill sets as graphs** where nodes are skills and edges are skill relations, using a **transformer-style graph architecture** to learn skill embeddings that capture complex inter-skill relationships. Demonstrated on simulation tasks and real quadruped robot navigation.

- Paper: [GSC: A graph-based skill composition framework for robot learning (ScienceDirect)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0921889024001714)
- OpenReview: [GSC](https://openreview.net/forum?id=bIymlpFVj1)

### RoboBallet (Science Robotics, Sep 2025)
Uses **GNN policies trained via RL** for multi-robot task and motion planning. The GNN captures inter-robot dependencies as a graph, enabling automated task allocation and scheduling under spatio-temporal constraints. While multi-robot rather than single-robot skill composition, the architecture (GNN for feasibility reasoning over sequences of actions) is highly transferable.

- Paper: [RoboBallet (Science Robotics)](https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/scirobotics.ads1204)

### Compositional Diffusion Transformer (2024-2025)
A **semantic compositional diffusion transformer** that factorizes transitions into robot-, object-, obstacle-, and objective-specific components. Trained on limited tasks, it zero-shot generates valid transitions for unseen task combinations, with validation via offline RL.

- Paper: [Iterative Compositional Data Generation for Robot Control (arXiv 2512.10891)](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.10891)

---

| Aspect | Maturity |
|--------|----------|
| Learned precondition/effect models for skill chaining | **High** -- multiple published methods (GSC diffusion, ConditionNET, relational preconditions) |
| Neural dynamics replacing analytical models | **Medium-High** -- SuperDyno (2025) is a clear demonstration for humanoids, but not yet widely adopted for task composition |
| GNN-based skill composition | **Medium** -- GSC (2024) is a clear proof of concept; RoboBallet shows industrial scale |
| Transformer-based skill sequence prediction | **Medium-High** -- Skill Transformer, MuST show strong results |

<result>I now have comprehensive information about the DemoHLM paper. Here is my detailed research report:

---

## DemoHLM: From One Demonstration to Generalizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

**arXiv: 2510.11258**
**Authors:** Yuhui Fu, Feiyang Xie, Chaoyi Xu, Jing Xiong, Haoqi Yuan, and Zongqing Lu

---

### What is DemoHLM?

DemoHLM is a framework that enables a humanoid robot to learn generalizable loco-manipulation skills from a **single teleoperated demonstration** captured in simulation. From that one demo, it automatically synthesizes hundreds to thousands of diverse successful trajectories by replaying the demonstration under varied initial conditions, then trains imitation learning policies on this synthetic data that transfer zero-shot to the real world.

---

### Pipeline Overview (Hierarchical Architecture)

DemoHLM uses a **two-level hierarchy**:

1. **Low-level universal whole-body controller** -- takes motion commands (linear velocities vx/vy, yaw rate omega, torso height/roll/pitch/yaw, upper-body joint targets) and outputs joint-level PD targets at 50 Hz, providing omnidirectional locomotion.

2. **High-level manipulation policy** -- learned via behavior cloning on the generated data, using visual feedback from an RGB-D camera to produce commands for the whole-body controller.

---

### Object-Centric Representation Conversion

The key insight enabling data generation from a single demo is converting the demonstration into **object-centric relative pose trajectories**:

- The demonstration is split at the **first contact time** (tc) into two segments.
- **Before contact (object-centric phase):** End-effector poses are expressed relative to the object: `T_obj_eef = T_eef * (T_obj_bar)^{-1}`. This means the approach trajectory is defined relative to the object, so when the object moves, the end-effector trajectory adapts accordingly.
- **After contact (proprioception-centric phase):** End-effector poses are expressed relative to the end-effector's pose at the contact moment: `T_pro_eef = T_eef * (T_eef_bar)_{tc}^{-1}`. This handles the manipulation phase where the hand remains roughly fixed relative to the object.

These relative representations allow the same demonstration to be "replayed" for arbitrary initial robot and object poses.

---

### The 3-Stage Trajectory Generation Pipeline

For each new randomized initial condition, a trajectory is generated in three stages:

1. **Locomotion Stage:** A PD controller generates velocity commands (vx, vy, omega_yaw) to navigate the robot's base from its random initial pose to a suitable starting position near the object. The stage terminates when distance and rotation thresholds are met.

2. **Pre-Manipulation Stage:** Using the object-centric representation, the system computes target end-effector poses as `T_eef = T_obj_eef * T_obj_bar`. An interpolation trajectory smoothly bridges any gap between the current end-effector pose (after locomotion) and the required starting pose for manipulation. This ensures the hand is correctly positioned relative to the object regardless of approach direction.

3. **Manipulation Stage:** Switches to the proprioception-centric representation. End-effector poses are computed as `T_eef = T_eef_bar * (T_pro_eef)^{-1}`. The controller executes the actual manipulation skill (lifting, pushing, grasping, etc.).

---

### VR Teleoperation Setup

- An **Apple Vision Pro** is used as the motion capture device via the VisionProTeleop system.
- It streams head and wrist poses, which are mapped to the G1's corresponding head and wrist links.
- Lower-body degrees of freedom remain fixed during collection.
- Multi-task inverse kinematics (using the **Pink library**) solves for full-body joint targets.

---

### Robot Platform

**Unitree G1 humanoid robot** equipped with:
- An RGB-D camera for visual feedback
- Both rubber-hand and gripper end-effectors (tested across different task sets)

---

### Experimental Results

**10 loco-manipulation tasks tested:**
- Rubber-hand tasks (4): LiftBox, PressCube, PushCube, Handover
- Gripper tasks (6): GraspCube, OpenCabinet, PushCart, EraseBoard, PourWater, ExchangeCube

**Data scaling:** Success rates increase monotonically with dataset size (100 to 5000 trajectories), with diminishing returns at larger scales. Example: LiftBox went from 86.41% (100 samples) to 98.83% (5000 samples).

**Behavior cloning architectures compared:**
- **ACT** (Action Chunking Transformers) and **Diffusion Policy** achieved comparable strong performance
- **MLP** with action chunking showed substantial drops, suggesting temporally expressive architectures are important

**Randomization regions (R1-R3):** Larger spatial randomization introduces more variability but reduces data generation success rates. R3 (largest) is used by default.

**Real-world validation:** 5 trials per task on the physical Unitree G1, demonstrating robust sim-to-real transfer.

---

### Limitations (Acknowledged by Authors)

1. **Sim-to-real gap:** Reliance on simulation-generated data can hinder real robot performance due to domain differences.
2. **Limited perception:** A single RGB-D camera may constrain performance in cluttered or occluded scenes.
3. **Object pose dependence:** Using FoundationPose for 6D object pose estimation limits manipulation to pre-modeled objects only (cannot handle unmodeled/novel objects).

---

### Relationship to Grammar-Based Compositional Task Generation

The paper does **not** mention or compare against grammar-based compositional task generation approaches. DemoHLM's approach is fundamentally different from grammar-based methods:

- **Grammar-based approaches** (e.g., task and motion planning with symbolic grammars) define tasks through compositional rules and symbolic primitives, generating diverse tasks by combining grammar elements.
- **DemoHLM** instead takes a **data-driven demonstration-centric** approach -- it does not compose new tasks from primitives but rather generates diverse *instances* of the same task by varying spatial configurations. The "diversity" is in the initial conditions and object placements, not in task structure.

DemoHLM is conceptually an extension of **MimicGen** (which worked only with fixed-base robot arms) to the full humanoid loco-manipulation setting, adding the locomotion stage and handling the unique challenges of whole-body control.

---

### Key Differentiators from Prior Work

| Prior approach | DemoHLM's advantage |
|---|---|
| RL with task-specific rewards (WoCoCo, etc.) | No reward engineering needed |
| Large real-world teleoperation datasets | Only one demo required |
| MimicGen (fixed-base arms) | Handles full humanoid locomotion + manipulation |
| SMPL-based motion retargeting | Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer |
| Hard-coded task definitions | Automatically generalizes from demonstration |

---

## Summary of Findings

This is an **active and rapidly maturing research area** (2023-2025), with multiple complementary approaches. There is clearly prior work here, but the space is not saturated -- especially for humanoid-specific applications and for learning dynamics predicates that replace analytical models like ZMP/centroidal dynamics.

## 1. Learned Models That Predict Whether a Skill Sequence Will Succeed

### Generative Skill Chaining (GSC) -- Mishra et al., 2024 (CoRL/arXiv)
The most directly relevant work. It trains **skill-level diffusion models** that capture the joint distribution of (precondition, skill parameters, effect) for each skill. At inference time, it samples valid skill chains by ensuring each skill's post-condition satisfies the next skill's precondition. This **implicitly predicts transition feasibility** -- if the chained sampling fails to find a valid configuration, the sequence is deemed infeasible.

- Paper: [Generative Skill Chaining: Long-Horizon Skill Planning with Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03360)
- Project: [https://generative-skill-chaining.github.io/](https://generative-skill-chaining.github.io/)

### SCaR: Refining Skill Chaining for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation (NeurIPS 2024)
Refines skill chaining with learned success predictors that determine whether sub-task transitions will lead to overall task success.

- Paper: [SCaR (NeurIPS 2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/ca92ff06d973ece92cecc561757d500e-Paper-Conference.pdf)

### Skill Transformer / MuST (Multi-Head Skill Transformer)
Transformers trained end-to-end on demonstration trajectories to predict both high-level skill selection and low-level actions. MuST maintains 80-90% success rates on 40 evaluation tasks and learns to select optimal skill orderings (e.g., "pick first" vs. "flip first") depending on object state.

- [Skill Transformer (arXiv 2308.09873)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09873)
- [MuST (Amazon Science)](https://cdn.amazon.science/fd/a2/6f07a8c241fcad2a93a5bb889428/must-multi-head-skill-transformer-for-long-horizon-dexterous-manipulation-with-skill-progress.pdf)

### ConditionNET (2025)
Learns preconditions and effects of actions in a **fully data-driven manner** using vision-language models, explicitly modeling dependencies between actions, preconditions, and effects for execution monitoring.

- Paper: [ConditionNET (arXiv 2502.01167)](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01167)

---

## 2. Approaches That Learn Transition Dynamics Between Primitives

### SuperDyno (ICLR 2025 Workshop)
**Directly relevant to your reviewer's suggestion.** Learns a differentiable neural dynamics model for humanoid whole-body control. Medium-sized neural networks serve as a differentiable simulator, providing smoother gradients than analytical simulators, enabling escape from local optima, and supporting domain transfer. This replaces analytical dynamics with learned ones.

- Paper: [SuperDyno: Scalable Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Differentiable Neural Network Dynamics](https://dynamics-humanoid.github.io/dynamics-humanoid/)
- OpenReview: [ICLR 2025 Workshop](https://openreview.net/forum?id=FPgKt7bA8w)

### SRSA: Skill Retrieval and Adaptation (2024)
Learns a **transfer success predictor** that takes source/target task features (geometry, dynamics, expert actions) as input and outputs zero-shot transfer success probability. This is essentially a learned feasibility classifier for skill reuse.

- Project: [SRSA](https://srsa2024.github.io/)

### Relational Learning for Skill Preconditions (CMU Robotics Institute)
Learns an **object-relation model** with continuous representations for pairwise object relations, trained in simulation and used by a separate precondition model to predict real-world skill preconditions. Generalizes to variable numbers of objects with different shapes/sizes.

- Paper: [Relational Learning for Skill Preconditions](https://www.ri.cmu.edu/publications/relational-learning-for-skill-preconditions/)

---

## 3. GNN and Transformer-Based Composition Feasibility Predictors

### GSC: Graph-based Skill Composition (Robotics and Autonomous Systems, Sep 2024)
The most directly relevant GNN-based work. Models **entire skill sets as graphs** where nodes are skills and edges are skill relations, using a **transformer-style graph architecture** to learn skill embeddings that capture complex inter-skill relationships. Demonstrated on simulation tasks and real quadruped robot navigation.

- Paper: [GSC: A graph-based skill composition framework for robot learning (ScienceDirect)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0921889024001714)
- OpenReview: [GSC](https://openreview.net/forum?id=bIymlpFVj1)

### RoboBallet (Science Robotics, Sep 2025)
Uses **GNN policies trained via RL** for multi-robot task and motion planning. The GNN captures inter-robot dependencies as a graph, enabling automated task allocation and scheduling under spatio-temporal constraints. While multi-robot rather than single-robot skill composition, the architecture (GNN for feasibility reasoning over sequences of actions) is highly transferable.

- Paper: [RoboBallet (Science Robotics)](https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/scirobotics.ads1204)

A **semantic compositional diffusion transformer** that factorizes transitions into robot-, object-, obstacle-, and objective-specific components. Trained on limited tasks, it zero-shot generates valid transitions for unseen task combinations, with validation via offline RL.
